messages:
jana-cs: Customer reported a crash when parsing JSON from our "structured" output mode. They say their parser throws a SyntaxError: Unexpected token ILLEGAL. Paste of the exact payload they tried:

customer_jdoe: "Posting the raw response we get from /v1/generate (streaming=true). It used to work, now our JSON.parse fails mid-file).

Here is the concatenated stream we received (we reassembled chunks client-side):

```
{
  \"id\": \"gen_abc123\",\n  \"items\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"Line1\\nLine2\\nC:\\\\path\\\\to\\\\file\\\"with\\\"quotes\\\"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```

When we call JSON.parse on that exact string we get SyntaxError. We suspect some control char or broken escaping. We only see this when streaming=true and data includes backslashes/quotes/newlines.

alex-eng: Thanks Jana — can you attach the request params they used (model, structured output flag, streaming) and whether they used a Redwood SDK or direct HTTP? Also which runtime (hosted/dedicated/private)?

jana-cs: Params from the customer:
- model: openlm-13b-v2
- mode: structured (json)
- stream: true
- client: custom node fetch, re-assembles chunks with `for await (const chunk of res.body)`
- environment: hosted (us-west)

mike-runtime: I believe I've seen this before. Hypothesis: chunk boundary splitting is dropping an escape backslash when a backslash and quote land on different chunks and we do incremental unescape on the server streaming layer. Example bad streaming chunk sequence we saw in a unit repro: 

Chunk A: `{\"text\": \"C:\\\\path\`
Chunk B: `\\\\to\\\\file\\\" }`

If the server-side streamer runs a partial unescape on each chunk then reassembly can lose a backslash, producing `C:\path\to\file\"` (invalid sequences) or prematurely-closed strings.

alex-eng: Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces for us? Customer provided this quick repro using the direct HTTP API:

```bash
curl -sS -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"openlm-13b-v2","stream":true,"prompt":"Respond in JSON: {\\\"path\\\":\\\"C:\\\\\\\\temp\\\\\\\\new\\nline\\\"}'}'
```

Customer says they then concat chunks naively and run JSON.parse on the result. Works if stream=false. Fails for stream=true.

mike-runtime: Ok this matches the chunk-boundary escape-stitching bug we tracked last quarter (we thought it was fixed). Likely regression in streaming encoder that tries to be "helpful" and decodes escapes per-chunk. Short-term mitigation: set stream=false or ensure client reconstructs raw binary stream and does not run partial decode on chunk boundaries.

jana-cs: Customer needs a safer workaround — they cannot disable streaming for bandwidth reasons. Any workaround we can recommend?

mike-runtime: Two options: 1) Have client treat stream as opaque binary and just concatenate raw bytes (do not run any per-chunk text decoding). In node streams that means using Buffer.concat on chunks rather than converting each chunk to string. 2) Use an escaping envelope in the prompt so generated JSON contains double-escaped backslashes (ugly but stable): e.g., in the prompt ask model to return `\\\\` where `\\` is expected, then reduce on client. We'll recommend option 1.

alex-eng: I'll escalate to eng-runtime. Mike, can you open a ticket with steps and a short repro? Include the curl above and a minimal streaming chunk log that demonstrates a lost backslash at the boundary.

mike-runtime: Created ticket INF-8421 and assigned to @alex-eng. Link: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-8421 (ops-bot auto-note: case INF-8421 created by mike-runtime).

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-8421 — "streaming: escape stitching drops backslash at chunk boundary causing invalid JSON". Priority: P1 (customer impact). Assigned: alex-eng.

alex-eng: Pinged eng-ml and eng-runtime on the ticket. Preliminary root-cause: streaming encoder attempts to decode escape sequences chunk-wise which is unsafe. Plan: revert the streaming unescape behavior and add a regression test that simulates split escape sequences across chunks. ETA: hotfix in next 4 hours for hosted; follow-up rollout to Dedicated/Private next week.

customer_jdoe: Thank you — customer can confirm workaround by setting their client to Buffer.concat chunks instead of chunk.toString() and it resolved the issue temporarily.

jana-cs: Marking as escalated — will update customer with hotfix ETA and workaround. :thumbsup:

alex-eng: Adding note for product: consider adding guidance to the docs about JSON/structured streaming and clients needing to concat raw bytes. I'll post a docs PR after hotfix.

mike-runtime: Also adding unit test in runtime repo: simulate chunk split between `\\` and `\"` and assert final output keeps both backslashes.

jana-cs: Closing loop — customer ok with workaround until hotfix is deployed. Will re-open if they see recurrence.

ops-bot: INF-8421 status updated: in-progress.

(reacts: :eyes: :white_check_mark: on some messages)
